dialogues.title: Introductions at a Dinner Party
dialogues.scene: Two guests meet for the first time at a friend's dinner party, moving from formal to informal address.

lines.speaker: Giulia
lines.target: Buonasera! Io sono Giulia. E Lei?
lines.ref: Good evening! I'm Giulia. And you?

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.target: Piacere, Giulia. Mi chiamo Marco.
lines.ref: Nice to meet you, Giulia. My name is Marco.

lines.speaker: Giulia
lines.target: Piacere mio! Come sta?
lines.ref: My pleasure! How are you?

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.target: Molto bene, grazie. Possiamo darci del tu?
lines.ref: Very well, thanks. Can we use 'tu' (informal)?

lines.speaker: Giulia
lines.target: Certo! Allora, di dove sei?
lines.ref: Of course! So, where are you from?

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.target: Sono di Napoli, ma vivo a Milano. E tu?
lines.ref: I'm from Naples, but I live in Milan. And you?

lines.speaker: Giulia
lines.target: Io sono di Firenze. Come conosci Paolo?
lines.ref: I'm from Florence. How do you know Paolo?

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.target: Siamo colleghi di lavoro. E tu?
lines.ref: We're work colleagues. And you?

lines.speaker: Giulia
lines.target: È un mio vecchio amico. Andiamo a tavola?
lines.ref: He's an old friend of mine. Shall we go to the table?

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.target: Volentieri, ho fame!
lines.ref: Gladly, I'm hungry!

vocab: darsi del tu (to switch to informal 'you')
di dove sei? (where are you from?)
dialogues.note: Italians switch from formal Lei to informal tu once a friendly rapport forms; 'Possiamo darci del tu?' is the polite way to propose the switch.

dialogues.title: At the Bar for Breakfast
dialogues.scene: A customer orders coffee and a pastry at a typical Italian bar.

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: Buongiorno! Un cappuccino e un cornetto, per favore.
lines.ref: Good morning! A cappuccino and a croissant, please.

lines.speaker: Barista
lines.target: Subito. Il cornetto lo vuole vuoto o con la crema?
lines.ref: Right away. Do you want the croissant plain or with cream?

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: Con la crema, grazie.
lines.ref: With cream, thanks.

lines.speaker: Barista
lines.target: Beve il cappuccino qui al banco o al tavolo?
lines.ref: Will you drink the cappuccino here at the counter or at a table?

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: Al banco, ho fretta.
lines.ref: At the counter, I'm in a hurry.

lines.speaker: Barista
lines.target: Ecco a Lei. Desidera altro?
lines.ref: Here you are. Would you like anything else?

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: No, così va bene. Quanto le devo?
lines.ref: No, that's fine. How much do I owe you?

lines.speaker: Barista
lines.target: Sono due euro e cinquanta.
lines.ref: That's two euros fifty.

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: Ecco. Grazie mille!
lines.ref: Here you go. Thank you very much!

lines.speaker: Barista
lines.target: Grazie a Lei, buona giornata!
lines.ref: Thank you, have a good day!

vocab: avere fretta (to be in a hurry)
Quanto le devo? (How much do I owe you?)
dialogues.note: In Italy, coffee costs less standing at the counter (al banco) than sitting at a table, where a service charge is usually added.

dialogues.title: Asking for Directions in Rome
dialogues.scene: A tourist asks a passer-by how to reach the Colosseum and nearby services.

lines.speaker: Turista
lines.target: Scusi, come si arriva al Colosseo?
lines.ref: Excuse me, how do you get to the Colosseum?

lines.speaker: Passante
lines.target: È facile. Vada sempre dritto fino al semaforo.
lines.ref: It's easy. Go straight ahead to the traffic light.

lines.speaker: Turista
lines.target: Sempre dritto, va bene. E poi?
lines.ref: Straight ahead, okay. And then?

lines.speaker: Passante
lines.target: Poi giri a destra e lo vedrà davanti a Lei.
lines.ref: Then turn right and you'll see it in front of you.

lines.speaker: Turista
lines.target: È lontano a piedi?
lines.ref: Is it far on foot?

lines.speaker: Passante
lines.target: No, dieci minuti circa.
lines.ref: No, about ten minutes.

lines.speaker: Turista
lines.target: C'è una fermata dell'autobus qui vicino?
lines.ref: Is there a bus stop near here?

lines.speaker: Passante
lines.target: Sì, dall'altra parte della strada.
lines.ref: Yes, on the other side of the street.

lines.speaker: Turista
lines.target: E una farmacia? Ho bisogno di un'aspirina.
lines.ref: And a pharmacy? I need an aspirin.

lines.speaker: Passante
lines.target: Ce n'è una accanto al bar.
lines.ref: There's one next to the café.

lines.speaker: Turista
lines.target: Grazie mille, molto gentile!
lines.ref: Thank you very much, very kind of you!

dialogues.note: When giving directions to strangers, Italians use the formal imperative (vada, giri), which is the Lei-form of the subjunctive.

dialogues.title: Buying Fresh Produce at the Market
dialogues.scene: A shopper buys fruit and vegetables at an open-air market, discussing quantity, price, and freshness.

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: Buongiorno, sono freschi questi pomodori?
lines.ref: Good morning, are these tomatoes fresh?

lines.speaker: Fruttivendolo
lines.target: Freschissimi, arrivati stamattina dalla campagna.
lines.ref: Very fresh, they arrived this morning from the countryside.

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: Perfetto. Ne prendo un chilo.
lines.ref: Perfect. I'll take a kilo of them.

lines.speaker: Fruttivendolo
lines.target: Ecco fatto. Le servono anche le zucchine?
lines.ref: Done. Do you also need some zucchini?

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: Sì, mezzo chilo. E le pesche, quanto costano?
lines.ref: Yes, half a kilo. And the peaches, how much are they?

lines.speaker: Fruttivendolo
lines.target: Due euro e cinquanta al chilo. Sono dolcissime.
lines.ref: Two fifty a kilo. They're very sweet.

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: Allora ne prendo sei, ma che siano mature.
lines.ref: Then I'll take six, but make sure they're ripe.

lines.speaker: Fruttivendolo
lines.target: Non si preoccupi, scelgo le migliori.
lines.ref: Don't worry, I'll pick the best ones.

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: La ringrazio. Quant'è in tutto?
lines.ref: Thank you. How much is it in total?

lines.speaker: Fruttivendolo
lines.target: Sono sette euro esatti.
lines.ref: That's exactly seven euros.

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: Ecco a Lei. Arrivederci!
lines.ref: Here you are. Goodbye!

vocab: Quant'è in tutto? (How much in total?)
dialogues.note: At Italian markets you usually shouldn't touch the produce yourself; you ask the vendor, who selects and weighs it for you.

dialogues.title: Booking a Table by Phone
dialogues.scene: A customer phones a restaurant to reserve a table, giving the day, time, number of guests, and a dietary need.

lines.speaker: Ristorante
lines.target: Ristorante Da Luigi, buonasera.
lines.ref: Da Luigi Restaurant, good evening.

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: Buonasera, vorrei prenotare un tavolo.
lines.ref: Good evening, I'd like to book a table.

lines.speaker: Ristorante
lines.target: Certo. Per quante persone?
lines.ref: Of course. For how many people?

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: Per quattro, sabato sera.
lines.ref: For four, Saturday evening.

lines.speaker: Ristorante
lines.target: A che ora preferisce?
lines.ref: What time do you prefer?

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: Verso le otto e mezza, se possibile.
lines.ref: Around half past eight, if possible.

lines.speaker: Ristorante
lines.target: Va benissimo. A che nome?
lines.ref: That's fine. Under what name?

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: A nome Bianchi. Una persona è vegetariana.
lines.ref: Under Bianchi. One person is vegetarian.

lines.speaker: Ristorante
lines.target: Nessun problema, abbiamo diversi piatti vegetariani.
lines.ref: No problem, we have several vegetarian dishes.

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: Ottimo. Avete un tavolo all'aperto?
lines.ref: Great. Do you have a table outside?

lines.speaker: Ristorante
lines.target: Sì, glielo riservo. A sabato!
lines.ref: Yes, I'll reserve it for you. See you Saturday!

dialogues.note: When booking, expect the question 'A che nome?' Italians give a surname, and 'A nome...' (under the name of...) is the standard reply.

dialogues.title: At the Pharmacy
dialogues.scene: A customer describes symptoms and asks the pharmacist for medicine and advice on dosage.

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: Buongiorno, non mi sento molto bene.
lines.ref: Good morning, I don't feel very well.

lines.speaker: Farmacista
lines.target: Mi dica, quali sono i sintomi?
lines.ref: Tell me, what are the symptoms?

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: Ho mal di gola e un po' di febbre da ieri.
lines.ref: I have a sore throat and a slight fever since yesterday.

lines.speaker: Farmacista
lines.target: Ha anche la tosse o il raffreddore?
lines.ref: Do you also have a cough or a cold?

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: Sì, tossisco soprattutto la notte.
lines.ref: Yes, I cough especially at night.

lines.speaker: Farmacista
lines.target: Le consiglio queste pastiglie e uno sciroppo.
lines.ref: I recommend these lozenges and a syrup.

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: Quante volte al giorno devo prenderle?
lines.ref: How many times a day should I take them?

lines.speaker: Farmacista
lines.target: Le pastiglie tre volte al giorno, dopo i pasti.
lines.ref: The lozenges three times a day, after meals.

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: E lo sciroppo?
lines.ref: And the syrup?

lines.speaker: Farmacista
lines.target: Un cucchiaio prima di dormire. Se la febbre sale, veda un medico.
lines.ref: A spoonful before sleeping. If the fever rises, see a doctor.

lines.speaker: Cliente
lines.target: Grazie, è stato molto gentile. Quanto le devo?
lines.ref: Thanks, you've been very kind. How much do I owe you?

lines.speaker: Farmacista
lines.target: Dodici euro. Guarisca presto!
lines.ref: Twelve euros. Get well soon!

dialogues.note: In Italy, pharmacists are highly trained and often give first advice for minor ailments; many medicines are kept behind the counter rather than on open shelves.
